data.name: Fahid
data.gender_notes: Fahid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘fahada’, meaning ‘to be quick, swift, or escape’. The name Fahid is often given to children born during moments of haste or urgency, reflecting the swift and efficient nature of the parents. The name Fahid carries the meaning “Quick, Swift” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fahid usually hope their child will grow to embody quick, swift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner strength and courage, often used for boys who are expected to grow up and lead
data.etymology: Fahid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Quick, Swift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fahid total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_english.name: Fahid
in_english.meaning: One who hears and understands, patient, and one who hears the sound
in_english.long_meaning: Fahid is a name that means one who hears and understands, patient, and one who hears the sound. This name is derived from the Arabic root word "f-h-d", which means to hear and understand. In Islamic tradition, Fahid is considered a noble name that signifies one who is patient, persistent, and has good hearing. This name is also associated with the qualities of being kind, gentle, and compassionate. In modern times, Fahid is used as a given name for boys in many Muslim cultures, including Arabic, Urdu, and Turkish speaking communities.

historical_references.reference: Fahid ibn Al-Jarrah was the first caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate, which ruled the Muslim world from Damascus between 661 and 750 AD. He was a successful military commander who rose to power after the death of Prophet Muhammad and the first caliph, Abu Bakr. Fahid played a crucial role in consolidating the early Islamic state and expanding its territories through military conquests.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Caliphate, early Islamic state, military conquests

historical_references.reference: Fahid bin Sahl was a renowned Sufi scholar and poet who lived during the Abbasid Caliphate era (750-1258 AD). He is best known for his work 'Al-Ghazl al-Farid', a treatise on the spiritual journey towards God. Fahid's teachings emphasized the importance of love and devotion towards God and the need to cleanse oneself of worldly desires to achieve spiritual enlightenment.
historical_references.context: Sufism, spiritual journey, love and devotion towards God
